- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are rising steadily, check for over-optimism — true outcomes often overshoot initial peaks then correct, especially after high-event days.
- If official event net supply is negative and sentiment is bearish, model forecasts tend to underestimate true price spikes — adjust upward by 2–5% for high-event periods.
- After a sharp spike in true outcome (e.g., >10% above prior 30d mean), model forecasts often lag by 1–3 days — apply a 1-day lag correction for subsequent forecasts.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and event supply is negative, model forecasts often overcorrect — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for 3–5 days.
- If event count is high and supply net is negative, true outcomes often exceed model forecasts by 5–15% — apply a 5–10% upward bias correction for 3–7 day horizons.
- For 30d forecasts, if sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes (e.g., 0.00 or -0.33), model forecasts may be too optimistic — reduce forecast mean by 3–8% for 3–5 day horizons.
- When sentiment is bullish but true outcome is volatile (e.g., 3+ spikes above 85), model forecasts often fail to capture volatility — add 1–2% volatility buffer to forecast range.
